title: Wake Up In New York, 29 October 1929

beats.narration: You wake up on Wall Street. By tonight, almost everyone you know will be broke.
beats.shot_prompt: First-person POV waking up in a cramped 1920s New York boarding house room, morning light through a dusty window, a folded newspaper on the wooden floor

beats.narration: It's Tuesday, October 29th, 1929. Five days ago the stock market cracked. Today it breaks completely.
beats.shot_prompt: POV walking down a crowded Wall Street in 1929, men in fedoras and overcoats hurrying, vintage cars honking, overcast sky, stone bank facades

beats.narration: So many shares change hands that the ticker tape runs hours behind. Nobody knows what anything is worth.
beats.shot_prompt: POV on a chaotic 1929 stock exchange trading floor, paper ticker tape piling up, traders shouting and waving slips, handheld camera pushing through the crowd

beats.narration: People who borrowed money to buy stocks lose everything by lunch. Crowds gather outside the banks.
beats.shot_prompt: POV in an anxious crowd outside a 1929 New York bank, people pressing toward closed doors, police officers holding them back, sepia tones

beats.narration: This is the start of the Great Depression. It will last about ten years.
beats.shot_prompt: POV standing on an empty Wall Street at dusk, newspapers blowing across the cobblestones, street lamps flickering on, melancholic mood

beats.narration: So, what would you have done with your money? Best answer picks where I take you tomorrow.
beats.shot_prompt: POV looking down at a 1929 newspaper lying on wet cobblestones at night, slow push in, lamplight reflections

facts_to_check: Black Thursday (24 October 1929) was five days earlier
Ticker tape ran hours behind due to record volume
Margin buyers were wiped out; crowds gathered at banks and the exchange
The Great Depression lasted roughly a decade
